targets.authors: Hu, M., & Nation, I. S. P.
targets.title: Unknown vocabulary density and reading comprehension
targets.evidence_quote: This study attempted to replicate and extend an influential study in vocabulary research in an underrepresented context and participant sample. One hundred and four Sri Lankan learners of L2 English, similar in vocabulary knowledge to the original sample in Hu and Nation (2000), responded to MCQs and SAQs on a narrative and an informational text in one of five vocabulary coverage conditions (80%, 90%, 95%, 98%, 100%).
targets.outcome_quote: Although it is impossible to link this difference in performance exclusively to the non-WEIRD features of our participants' context, the original findings from a smaller university-educated population were only partly replicated with the nonacademic learners in Sri Lanka, despite their having met the same screening criterion of a vocabulary-size threshold.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly characterize the original findings as only partly replicated; the linear relationship was confirmed but the 98% threshold was not.

reasoning: New Sri Lankan sample re-tests Hu and Nation (2000). The 1999 thesis describes the same original study rather than a second independent original paper; other coverage studies are background.
